The problem

## Australia has no way for pet owners to find clinical trials.

In the United States, the AVMA Veterinary Clinical Trials Registry, AniTrial, and the Dog Aging Project connect pet owners with hundreds of active studies. Dog and cat owners there can access new cancer immunotherapy, longevity drugs like rapamycin, and novel treatments for kidney disease, epilepsy, and arthritis.

In Australia, clinical research is fragmented across seven veterinary schools with no centralised, owner-accessible registry. Pet owners have no way to discover if a trial relevant to their pet's condition exists. They cannot enrol. Research teams struggle to recruit participants.

PetTrials fixes that. For free.

#### No centralised trial registry

Unlike the US, which has the AVMA registry with hundreds of active studies, Australian pet owners have nowhere to search for trials.

#### Research fragmented across 7 vet schools

UQ, Sydney, Melbourne, Murdoch, CSU, JCU, and Adelaide each run independent studies with no shared recruitment platform.

#### Researchers cannot find participants

Veterinary clinical trials depend on owner participation. Without a matching platform, recruitment is slow and studies are underpowered.

#### Pets miss out on life-saving treatments

Pets with cancer, chronic disease, or age-related conditions could benefit from new therapies, but only if their owners knew the trials existed.

### Why join a clinical trial?

  * Access novel treatments not yet available at regular vets
  * Free or subsidised veterinary care during the study
  * Close monitoring by specialist veterinary researchers
  * Contribute to research that helps all animals, and humans too
  * Your pet's full health profile in one secure place
  * Withdraw at any time. Participation is always voluntary

For pet owners

## Your pet's health history, in one place.

Even if there is no trial available for your pet right now, PetTrials gives you something no other Australian platform offers: a centralised, secure digital health record for your dog or cat.

Upload vaccinations, diagnoses, medications, and surgical history. Track changes over time. Share your profile with any vet. And when a trial does open that matches your pet's condition, you will be the first to know.

Think of it as a health passport for your pet, built for the future of veterinary medicine.

# Register your interest in our dog cancer trial

We are recruiting dogs with mast cell cancer in Australia for an investigational trial of personalised mRNA cancer vaccines. Register your interest and share a few details about your dog. Our team will contact you about further screening.

Why we are running this trial

## From Rosie’s story to a future for more dogs.

Image: Rosie

Rosie

The first dog treated with a personalised neoantigen vaccine.

It began with Rosie. Her experience with a personalised neoantigen vaccine encouraged Paul to explore how this approach could one day be made available to every dog with cancer.

Before an approach like this can become broadly available, we must study it carefully and support it by evidence for review by the relevant veterinary regulators. This clinical trial is an important step in that process, helping us learn from participating dogs and understand the vaccine more fully.

Read Rosie’s personalised mRNA cancer-vaccine story  →

Who can register

## If your dog has cancer and is currently in Australia, you’re welcome to register your interest. Our team will check whether your dog may be eligible for this trial.

Register your interest  →

## What this trial is looking at

The trial will investigate a personalised mRNA vaccine approach for dogs with mast cell cancer. Tell us about your dog and our team will help determine whether they may be eligible for screening.

Image

Dogs diagnosed with mast cell cancer who are based in, or able to travel within, Australia.

Every case is reviewed individually

A therapeutic mRNA vaccine designed from each dog’s own tumour and blood samples, intended to work alongside—not replace—existing care.

We help coordinate records, screening, sample logistics and updates, working with the trial team and your treating veterinarian.

## Clinical Trials Now Enrolling

#### CALL FOR PATIENTS: Clinical Trial for Soft Tissue Sarcoma in Dogs

Study Title: Feasibility and dose-optimization clinical trial of local immunotherapy for solid tumors in canine cancer patients

Eligibility: Any dog weighing 5kg or above with at least one cutaneous soft tissue sarcoma lesion that is greater than 1.7cm in diameter is eligible to enroll. All dogs that meet the study criteria will receive the study drug (no placebo) followed by surgical removal of the tumor 1 week later.

Study Purpose: This clinical trial evaluates the safety, feasibility, and biological effects of a newly designed immunotherapy. Specifically, the study is evaluating the injection of investigational T-cell engagers (TCEs) directly into tumors (intratumorally) in canine patients with soft tissue sarcoma (STS). TCEs are engineered antibodies that physically connect T cells to cancer cells by targeting specific markers (CD3 or CD28 on T cells, and B7-H3 or PD-L1 on cancer cells), triggering the immune system to destroy tumor cells.

# Ensaios clínicos autorizados

Publicado em 21/09/2020 00:00 Modificado em 03/03/2026 11:59

A Anvisa disponibiliza ferramenta para consulta de informações detalhadas sobre ensaios clínicos autorizados pela Agência. O serviço oferece ao público informações sobre a situação atual de cada ensaio clínico, além de informar os centros onde os ensaios clínicos foram autorizados e os respectivos investigadores responsáveis.

Mas atenção! A Anvisa só autoriza ensaios clínicos para apoiar o registro de medicamentos. Por isso, pesquisas científicas ou tecnológicas que não tenham essa finalidade não estão sujeitas à anuência da Agência e, portanto, não serão encontradas na ferramenta de consultas.

Dividida por áreas, a página de Consultas disponibiliza as seguintes categorias:

  * Documentos
  * Empresas e fiscalização de produtos

  * Informações regulatórias
  * Produtos

Na página de consultas, na área de Produtos, o interessado deverá clicar no ícone Ensaios Clínicos:

A ferramenta é intuitiva e o interessado escolhe quais são os critérios de consulta no início da busca. Preenchidos os campos, a página disponibiliza as informações que constam na base de dados de pesquisa clínica de medicamentos e produtos biológicos da Anvisa (Sistema de Controle de Pesquisa Clínica – SCPC). A área técnica está revisando e atualizando os dados do SCPC, de modo que eventuais incorreções sejam prontamente corrigidas.

Para auxiliar na busca, há um manual que explica passo a passo como a consulta pode ser realizada.

  * Manual de instruções para utilização da consulta

A consulta de pesquisas clínicas autorizadas não produz efeitos legais.

# Find a clinical trial

Search for a clinical trial in our online registry, or find out about other websites and registries that provide information about clinical trials.

## Search the online registry

Use our search function to start looking for a clinical trial. All clinical trials displayed on this website are sourced from the Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (ANZCTR). The ANZCTR includes all clinical trials with a recruitment site in Australia that are registered on ANZCTR as well as ClinicalTrials.gov, the US clinical trials registry.

## Other registries

There are other clinical trial registries that provide information on trials in Australia, New Zealand and, in some cases, other countries.

Each site will explain how to search the site for trials by the disease or condition that you are interested in. Some websites also allow you to register your details so you can:

  * receive information on potentially suitable trials when they become available
  * allow researchers to access your information and approach you directly.

### Registry list

The International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (ICTRP) aims to provide a single point of access to information about ongoing and completed clinical trials provided by registries around the world. ANZCTR is one of these registries.

The following Australian websites include listings of clinical trials specific to their 
area of expertise:

  * Australian Cancer Trials
  * Black Dog Institute
  * Cancer Institute NSW
  * GenesisCare
  * Growing Minds Australia
  * Icon Cancer Centre
  * MS Australia Clinical Trials Network
  * Nucleus Network
  * Pulmonary Fibrosis Australasian Clinical Trials Network
  * Victorian Cancer Trials Link (VCTL)

Additional sites providing clinical research information:

  * Australian Lung Foundation
  * Cancer Research Network
  * Cancer Trials Australia
  * Medicines Australia

## Talk to people

You can also find out about clinical trials by talking to a range of people. Learn who you can talk to for information about clinical trials relevant to you.

# Clinical trials

The School of Veterinary Science has several clinical trials and research studies seeking volunteers and input from the public.

Each trial or research study has varying requirements in regards to the assistance the investigators are requiring. We invite you to take a look at the current trials listed below to see if you can contribute.

Please note that all clinical trials and research have animal ethics and/or human ethics approvals, participation is voluntary and any participants can be removed from a trial at any time.

## Dog bone cancer vaccine trial

We are looking for pet dogs diagnosed with cancer to test an experimental vaccine. The clinical research trial is for dogs recently diagnosed with canine appendicular osteosarcoma, a common bone tumour that affects 10,000 dogs a year globally. In this trial, our researchers will assess two vaccine formulations. To be eligible, dogs need to have been diagnosed with appendicular osteosarcoma of long bones of the limbs with no evidence of metastasis, or cancer spread, based on a physical exam and radiographs.

# Dogs with cancer could leave lasting legacy

6 February 2026

Image: A female and male academic kneel down with a cavoodle on the grass

Professor Rachel Allavena and Dr José Granados Soler urge owners of eligible dogs to apply for the trial.

(Photo credit: The University of Queensland )

A University of Queensland project could be a glimmer of hope for dogs suffering from inoperable or incurable cancers.

The project will test the effectiveness of immunomodulatory drug Enzistat in treating solid tumours caused by naturally occurring cancers, including soft tissue sarcoma, mast cell tumour and melanoma.

Professor Rachel Allavena from UQ’s School of Veterinary Science said owners who had been told their dog’s cancer was terminal or their pet’s tumours were inoperable should apply for the trial.

“The 6-week treatment consists of oral tablet Enzistat being administered twice daily, regular consultations, blood samples and biopsies,” Professor Allavena said.

本臨床試験では、対象症例ごとにがんオルガノイドスクリーニング検査を実施し、有効性の期待される分子標的薬の投与を行い、その有効性と安全性を検証します。本臨床試験は、2025年6月に東京大学附属動物医療センター臨床試験委員会で承認を受けました。

### 対象

  * 根治的な標準治療の確立されていない犬猫の固形腫瘍症例(具体的な腫瘍種の例としてはリンパ腫や白血病などの血液腫瘍を除く、上皮系腫瘍(扁平上皮癌、腺癌、移行上皮癌、未分化癌など)、非上皮系腫瘍(軟部組織肉腫(線維肉腫、脂肪肉腫、平滑筋肉腫、横紋筋肉腫、血管肉腫、末梢神経鞘腫、滑膜肉腫など)、悪性黒色腫、中皮腫、肥満細胞腫など)、神経内分泌腫瘍(インスリノーマ、ガストリノーマ、ケモデクトーマ、脳腫瘍など)など) (計測可能な標的病変を有すること)
  * がんオルガノイドスクリーニング検査を実施し、有効性の期待される薬剤が特定された症例
  * 東京大学附属動物医療センターに通院できる飼い主様 (試験開始後、1, 3, 5週目の通院が必要になります。)
  * 治療効果検証のための病変の採材にご協力頂ける飼い主様

### 内容

  * ご自宅にて内服薬を投与していただきます。
  * 投与開始後、1, 3, 5週目に当院を受診し、副作用および効果を調べます。
  * 当院受診時には、一般検査(身体検査、血液検査、画像検査など)を実施し、有効性や安全性の評価をします。

# 〖臨床研究〗猫の口腔扁平上皮がんで症例募集中！

2025年8月18日

## 概要

ペットのがん治療には、手術、抗がん剤、放射線治療があります。放射線治療は、腫瘍に直接放射線を当てる方法ですが、腫瘍内が低酸素状態だと効果が下がることがあります。「レブリチン」は2023年に承認された世界初の動物用放射線増感剤で、腫瘍内の酸素を一時的に増やし、放射線治療の効果を高めます。岐阜大学動物病院では、猫の口腔扁平上皮がんに対して、放射線治療とレブリチンの併用による臨床研究を行っています。

## 対象

猫の口腔扁平上皮がん

## 試験内容

  * 5日間の放射線治療中にレブリチンを使用
  * 放射線治療後1・3・6か月後に経過確認のため来院の必要あり

## 治療費について

通常の治療費は発生しますが、レブリチンの薬剤費は無料です。
